Flag Partial Differential Equations and

Representations of Lie Algebras11 1 2000 Mathematical Subject Classification. Primary 17B30, 35F15, 35G15; Secondary 35C15, 35Q58

Abstract

In this paper, we solve the initial value problems of variable-coefficient generalized wave equations associated with trees and a large family of linear constant-coefficient partial differential equation by algebraic methods. Moreover, we find all the polynomial solutions for a 3-dimensional variable-coefficient flag partial differential equation of any order, the linear wave equation with dissipation and the generalized anisymmetrical Laplace equation. Furthermore, the polynomial-trigonometric solutions of a generalized Klein-Gordan equation associated with 3-dimensional generalized Tricomi operator ∂x2+x∂y2+y∂z2\partial_{x}^{2}+x\partial_{y}^{2}+y\partial_{z}^{2} are also given. As applications to representations of Lie algebras, we find certain irreducible polynomial representations of the Lie algebras s​l​(n,𝔽),s​o​(n,𝔽)sl(n,\mathbb{F}),\;so(n,\mathbb{F}) and the simple Lie algebra of type G2G_{2}.

1 Introduction

Barros-Neto and Gel’fand [BG1,BG2] (1998, 2002) studied solutions of the equation

ux​x+x​uy​y=δ⁡(x−x0,y−y0)u_{xx}+xu_{yy}=\delta(x-x_{0},y-y_{0}) (1.1)

related to the Tricomi operator ∂x2+x∂y2\partial_{x}^{2}+x\partial_{y}^{2}. A natural generalization of the Tricomi operator is ∂x12+x1∂x22+⋯+xn−1∂xn2\partial_{x_{1}}^{2}+x_{1}\partial_{x_{2}}^{2}+\cdots+x_{n-1}\partial_{x_{n}}^{2}. The equation

ut=ux1​x1+ux2​x2+⋯+uxn​xnu_{t}=u_{x_{1}x_{1}}+u_{x_{2}x_{2}}+\cdots+u_{x_{n}x_{n}} (1.2)

is the well known classical heat conduction equation related to the Laplacian operator ∂x12+∂x22+⋯+∂xn2\partial_{x_{1}}^{2}+\partial_{x_{2}}^{2}+\cdots+\partial_{x_{n}}^{2}. As pointed out in [BG1, BG2], the Tricomi operator is an analogue of the Laplacian operator. In [X2], we have solved the following natural analogue of heat conduction equation:

ut=ux1​x1+x1​ux2​x2+⋯+xn−1​uxn​xn.u_{t}=u_{x_{1}x_{1}}+x_{1}u_{x_{2}x_{2}}+\cdots+x_{n-1}u_{x_{n}x_{n}}. (1.3)

Indeed we have solved analogous heat conduction equations related to more general generalized Tricomi operators associated with tree graphs.

A tree 𝒯{\cal T} consists of a finite set of nodes 𝒩={ι1,ι2,…,ιn}{\cal N}=\{\iota_{1},\iota_{2},...,\iota_{n}\} and a set of edges

ℰ⊂{(ιi,ιj)∣1≤i<j≤n}{\cal E}\subset\{(\iota_{i},\iota_{j})\mid 1\leq i<j\leq n\} (1.4)

such that for each node ιi∈𝒩\iota_{i}\in{\cal N}, there exists a unique sequence {ιi1,ιi2,…,ιir}\{\iota_{i_{1}},\iota_{i_{2}},...,\iota_{i_{r}}\} of nodes with 1=i1<i2<⋯<ir−1<ir=i1=i_{1}<i_{2}<\cdots<i_{r-1}<i_{r}=i for which

(ιi1,ιi2),(ιi2,ιi3),…,(ιir−2,ιir−1),(ιir−1,ιir)∈ℰ.(\iota_{i_{1}},\iota_{i_{2}}),(\iota_{i_{2}},\iota_{i_{3}}),...,(\iota_{i_{r-2}},\iota_{i_{r-1}}),(\iota_{i_{r-1}},\iota_{i_{r}})\in{\cal E}. (1.5)

We also denote the tree 𝒯=(𝒩,ℰ){\cal T}=({\cal N},{\cal E}). For a tree 𝒯=(𝒩,ℰ){\cal T}=({\cal N},{\cal E}), we call the differential operator

d𝒯=∂x12+∑(ιi,ιj)∈ℰxi∂xj2d_{\cal T}=\partial_{x_{1}}^{2}+\sum_{(\iota_{i},\iota_{j})\in{\cal E}}x_{i}\partial_{x_{j}}^{2} (1.6)

a generalized Tricomi operator of type 𝒯{\cal T}. In [X2], we have solved the following analogue of heat conduction equation:

ut=d𝒯​(u)u_{t}=d_{\cal T}(u) (1.7)

subject to the initial condition:

u⁡(0,x1,…,xn)=f⁡(x1,…,xn)for​xi∈[−ai,ai],u(0,x_{1},...,x_{n})=f(x_{1},...,x_{n})\qquad\mbox{for}\;\;x_{i}\in[-a_{i},a_{i}], (1.8)

where ff is a given continuous function and aia_{i} are given positive real constants.

The equation

ut​t−ux1​x1−ux2​x2−⋯−uxn​xn=0u_{tt}-u_{x_{1}x_{1}}-u_{x_{2}x_{2}}-\cdots-u_{x_{n}x_{n}}=0 (1.9)

is the well-known wave equation associated with the Laplace operator ∂x12+∂x22+⋯+∂xn2\partial_{x_{1}}^{2}+\partial_{x_{2}}^{2}+\cdots+\partial_{x_{n}}^{2}. One of our goals in this paper is to solve the generalized wave equation

ut​t−d𝒯​(u)=0u_{tt}-d_{\cal T}(u)=0 (1.10)

subject to the initial conditions:

u⁡(0,x1,…,xn)=g0​(x1,…,xn),ut​(0,x1,…,xn)=g1​(x1,…,xn)u(0,x_{1},...,x_{n})=g_{0}(x_{1},...,x_{n}),\;\;\;u_{t}(0,x_{1},...,x_{n})=g_{1}(x_{1},...,x_{n}) (1.11)

for xi∈[−ai,ai]x_{i}\in[-a_{i},a_{i}], where g1,g2g_{1},g_{2} are given continuous functions and aia_{i} are given positive real constants. This is done by using our results in [X2] and an algebraic method of solving the following differential equation of flag type:

(d1+f1​d2+f2​d3+⋯+fn−1​dn)​(u)=0,(d_{1}+f_{1}d_{2}+f_{2}d_{3}+\cdots+f_{n-1}d_{n})(u)=0, (1.12)

where d1,d2,…,dnd_{1},d_{2},...,d_{n} are certain commuting locally nilpotent differential operators on the polynomial algebra ℝ⁡[x1,x2,…,xn]\mathbb{R}[x_{1},x_{2},...,x_{n}] and f1,…,fn−1f_{1},...,f_{n-1} are polynomials satisfying

di​(fj)=0if​i>j.d_{i}(f_{j})=0\qquad\mbox{if}\;\;i>j. (1.13)

Another slightly adjusted method enables us to solve a large family of linear constant-coefficient partial differential equations subject to initial conditions easily. This family contains almost all well-known linear constant-coefficient partial differential equations such as the Helmholtz equation and the Klein-Gordon equation. A general equation in this family can not be solved by separation of variables.

Polynomial solutions of linear partial differential equations are important for many reasons. For instance, polynomial solutions of Laplace equations are called harmonic polynomials, which are fundamental objects in differential geometry and analysis. In this paper, we have used our algebraic methods to find a basis of the space of all polynomial solutions for the following differential equations: (1)

∂xm1(u)+xn1​∂ym2(u)+yn2​∂zm3(u)=0,\partial_{x}^{m_{1}}(u)+x^{n_{1}}\partial_{y}^{m_{2}}(u)+y^{n_{2}}\partial_{z}^{m_{3}}(u)=0, (1.14)

where m1,m2,m3m_{1},m_{2},m_{3} are positive integers and n1,n2n_{1},n_{2} are nonnegative integers; (2) the linear wave equation with dissipation:

ut​t+ut−ux1​x1−ux2​x2−⋯−uxn​xn=0;u_{tt}+u_{t}-u_{x_{1}x_{1}}-u_{x_{2}x_{2}}-\cdots-u_{x_{n}x_{n}}=0; (1.15)

(3)

ut​t+λt​ut−ϵ⁡(ux1​x1+ux2​x2+⋯+uxn​xn)=0,u_{tt}+\frac{\lambda}{t}u_{t}-\epsilon(u_{x_{1}x_{1}}+u_{x_{2}x_{2}}+\cdots+u_{x_{n}x_{n}})=0, (1.16)

where ϵ∈{1,−1}\epsilon\in\{1,-1\} and λ\lambda is a nonzero real constant. When m1=m2=m3=2m_{1}=m_{2}=m_{3}=2 and n1=n2=0n_{1}=n_{2}=0, (1.14) is exactly the 3-dimensional Laplace equation. If ϵ=−1\epsilon=-1, (1.16) is the generalized anisymmetrical Laplace equation (cf. [A]). Moreover, the special Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation:

ut​t−ux1​x1−ux2​x2−⋯−uxn​xn−m⁡(m+1)t2​u=0u_{tt}-u_{x_{1}x_{1}}-u_{x_{2}x_{2}}-\cdots-u_{x_{n}x_{n}}-\frac{m(m+1)}{t^{2}}u=0 (1.17)

can be changed into a equation of type (1.16) with ϵ=1\epsilon=1. Furthermore, we have found the polynomial-trigonometric solutions of the generalized Klein-Gordan equation

ut​t−ux​x−x​uy​y−y​uz​z+a2​u=0u_{tt}-u_{xx}-xu_{yy}-yu_{zz}+a^{2}u=0 (1.18)

associated with 3-dimensional generalized Tricomi operator ∂x2+x∂y2+y∂z2\partial_{x}^{2}+x\partial_{y}^{2}+y\partial_{z}^{2}.

Flag partial differential equations also naturally appear in the representation theory of Lie algebras. Let 𝒢{\cal G} be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra with the Cartan root-space decomposition:

𝒢=ℋ⊕⨁α∈Φ𝒢α.{\cal G}={\cal H}\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}{\cal G}_{\alpha}. (1.19)

Suppose that MM is a finite-dimensional 𝒢{\cal G}-module. Take a weight-vector basis {v1,…,vn}\{v_{1},...,v_{n}\} of MM. Write

ξ⁡(vi)=∑j=1nρi,j​(ξ)​vjfor​ξ∈𝒢.\xi(v_{i})=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\rho_{i,j}(\xi)v_{j}\qquad\mbox{for}\;\;\xi\in{\cal G}. (1.20)

We define an action of 𝒢{\cal G} on ℝ⁡[x1,…,xn]\mathbb{R}[x_{1},...,x_{n}] by

ξ⁡(g)=∑i,j=1nρi,j​(ξ)​xj​∂xi(g)for​ξ∈𝒢,g∈ℝ⁡[x1,…,xn].\xi(g)=\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\rho_{i,j}(\xi)x_{j}\partial_{x_{i}}(g)\qquad\mbox{for}\;\;\xi\in{\cal G},\;g\in\mathbb{R}[x_{1},...,x_{n}]. (1.21)

Then ℝ⁡[x1,…,xn]\mathbb{R}[x_{1},...,x_{n}] forms a 𝒢{\cal G}-module isomorphic to the symmetric tensor S⁡(M)S(M) over MM. Take a base Π\Pi of the root system Φ\Phi and 0≠ξα∈𝒢α0\neq\xi_{\alpha}\in{\cal G}_{\alpha} for α∈Π\alpha\in\Pi. According to Weyl’s theorem of completely reducibility, ℝ⁡[x1,…,xn]\mathbb{R}[x_{1},...,x_{n}] can be decomposed as a direct sum of irreducible 𝒢{\cal G}-submodules. Such a decomposition is completely determined by the polynomial solutions (singular vectors or highest-weight vectors) of the following system of flag partial differential equations:

∑i,j=1nρi,j​(ξα)​xj​∂xi(u)=0,α∈Π.\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}\rho_{i,j}(\xi_{\alpha})x_{j}\partial_{x_{i}}(u)=0,\qquad\alpha\in\Pi. (1.22)

As simple applications of our algebraic methods of solving differential equations, we find a basis for certain irreducible polynomial representations of the Lie algebras s​l​(n,𝔽),s​o​(n,𝔽)sl(n,\mathbb{F}),\;so(n,\mathbb{F}) and the simple Lie algebra of type G2G_{2}.

In Section 2, we will present our algebraic methods and find all polynomial solutions of the above concerned partial differential equations. Section 3 is devoted to solve two initial value problems we mentioned in the above. In Section 4, certain polynomial representations of Lie algebras will be given.

Consider the wave equation in Riemannian space with a nontrivial conformal group (cf. [I1]):

ut​t−ux1​x1−∑i,j=2ngi,j​(x1−t)​uxi​xj=0,u_{tt}-u_{x_{1}x_{1}}-\sum_{i,j=2}^{n}g_{i,j}(x_{1}-t)u_{x_{i}x_{j}}=0, (2.25)

where we assume that gi,j​(z)g_{i,j}(z) are one-variable polynomials. Change variables:

z0=x1+t,z1=x1−t.z_{0}=x_{1}+t,\qquad z_{1}=x_{1}-t. (2.26)

Then
